{{Short description|Type of number in combinatorial mathematics}}
In [[combinatorics|combinatorial mathematics]], the '''Lobb number''' ''L''<sub>''m'',''n''</sub> counts the ways that ''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;''m'' open parentheses and ''n''&nbsp;−&nbsp;''m'' close parentheses can be arranged to form the start of a valid sequence of [[Dyck language|balanced parentheses]].<ref>{{Cite journal
| last1 = Koshy
| first1 = Thomas
| title = Lobb's generalization of Catalan's parenthesization problem
| journal = [[College Mathematics Journal|The College Mathematics Journal]]
| volume = 40
| issue = 2
| pages = 99–107
|date=March 2009
| doi = 10.4169/193113409X469532
}}</ref>

Lobb numbers form a natural generalization of the [[Catalan number]]s, which count the complete strings of balanced parentheses of a given length. Thus, the ''n''th Catalan number equals the Lobb number ''L''<sub>0,''n''</sub>.<ref>{{cite book
| last1 = Koshy
| first1 = Thomas
| title= Catalan Numbers with Applications
| year = 2008
| publisher = Oxford University Press
| isbn = 978-0-19-533454-8
}}</ref> They are named after Andrew Lobb, who used them  to give a simple [[mathematical induction|inductive proof]] of the formula for the ''n''<sup>th</sup> Catalan number.<ref>{{Cite journal
| last1 = Lobb
| first1 = Andrew
| title = Deriving the ''n''th Catalan number
| journal = [[Mathematical Gazette]]
| volume = 83
| issue = 8
| pages = 109–110
|date=March 1999
| doi = 10.2307/3618696
| jstor = 3618696
| s2cid = 126311995
}}</ref>

The Lobb numbers are parameterized by two non-negative [[integers]] ''m'' and ''n'' with ''n''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;''m''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0.  The (''m'',&nbsp;''n'')<sup>th</sup> Lobb number ''L''<sub>''m'',''n''</sub> is given in terms of [[binomial coefficient]]s by the formula
:<math>L_{m,n} = \frac{2m+1}{m+n+1}\binom{2n}{m+n} \qquad\text{ for }n \ge m \ge 0.</math>

An alternative expression for Lobb number ''L''<sub>''m'',''n''</sub> is:
:<math>L_{m,n} = \binom{2n}{m+n} - \binom{2n}{m+n+1} .</math>

The triangle of these numbers starts as {{OEIS|A039599}}
:<math>\begin{array}{rrrrrr}
1 \\
1 & 1 \\
2 & 3 & 1 \\
5 & 9 & 5 & 1\\
14 & 28 & 20 & 7 & 1\\
42 & 90 & 75 &35 & 9 & 1\\
\end{array}</math>
where the diagonal is
:<math>L_{n,n}=1,</math>
and the left column are the Catalan Numbers
:<math>L_{0,n}= \frac{1}{1+n}\binom{2n}{n}.</math>

As well as counting sequences of parentheses, the Lobb numbers also count the ways in which ''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;''m'' copies of the value +1 and ''n''&nbsp;−&nbsp;''m'' copies of the value −1 may be arranged into a sequence such that all of the [[partial sum]]s of the sequence are non-negative.

==Ballot counting==
The combinatorics of parentheses is replaced with counting ballots in an election with two candidates in [[Bertrand's ballot theorem]], first published by [[William Allen Whitworth]] in 1878. The theorem states the [[probability]] that winning candidate is ahead in the count, given known final tallies for each candidate.
